title: Clinical predictors for etiology of acute diarrhea in children in resource-limited settings
summary: Random forests screened clinical predictors and random-forest/logistic-regression models predicted viral versus other known pediatric diarrhea etiologies in GEMS data. Five factors yielded cross-validated AUC 0.825 (sensitivity 0.59, specificity 0.85); this retrospective analysis does not establish bedside benefit.
ai_technology: Random-forest feature screening and random-forest/logistic-regression models predict viral diarrhea etiology.

evidence.tested: Five clinical factors yielded cross-validated AUC 0.825 for viral etiology (sensitivity 0.59, specificity 0.85) using molecular-attribution reference data.
evidence.unknown: The model was retrospectively evaluated with five-fold cross-validation; no prospective clinical benefit was tested.
